posture: The withdrawal statement in TransferCircuit does not tie the spent note to the Merkle leaf, and it does not tie the nullifier to the leaf position. Any prover who knows one public path under a registered root can therefore drain Pool with fresh nullifiers; PoCs 1 and 2 show forged Groth16 proofs verifying. Trust also rests on a single-party groth16.Setup whose proving key is discarded, an owner who adds roots and swaps the verifier at will, and a committed Verifier.sol that is a placeholder. Pool's verifier interface does not match the gnark-generated verifier, so withdrawals revert against a real verifier today, which hides the soundness bugs rather than fixing them. SigCircuit has no on-chain consumer; its emulated limb check and the off-curve R question matter only once something consumes it. The most important action is to compute the leaf as a commitment to (Secret, In.Value, In.Owner) and derive Merkle direction bits from Index before any verifier is deployed.
out_of_scope: Solidity beyond the ZK integration (general Pool.sol logic) was reviewed only through lenses I1-I3; no solidity-auditor companion was available.
The deployed verifier, verifying key and setup ceremony are not in the repository; items depending on them are in Needs validation.
No Circom or Noir sources are present.
A runnable PoC for SigCircuit|Sig.R|point-not-on-curve was not built in this run; the item stays in Needs validation.

records.title: Merkle leaf is not bound to the spent note
records.description: Any prover proves membership of any public leaf, because the circuit never computes the leaf from Secret, In.Value and In.Owner.
records.proof: Path=[0x1eaf,11,22,33] with Root computed natively (MiMC, cur then sibling); Secret=1 and Secret=2, Index=1, Nullifier=MiMC(Secret,1), In.Value=Out.Value=2^64-1, owners 0, Fees=[0,1], Recipient=0xbeef, Extra=[0,0]. Both witnesses solve with honest hints and both Groth16 proofs verify against the same Root with different nullifiers.
records.impact: Any prover without a deposit drains Pool in withdrawals of up to 2^64-1 wei each, using fresh nullifiers against any registered root.

gates.executes: No constraint compares Path[0] with any hash of Secret, In.Value or In.Owner (transfer.go:50-56); every other assertion holds with q=1 and change=0.
gates.reachable: Any prover assigns these witnesses; the path data for a registered root is public tree data.
gates.unprivileged: Pool.withdraw is callable by anyone; no designated prover.
gates.impact: The verifier accepts withdrawals for notes that were never deposited; Pool.sol:51 pays value.

fix.summary: Compute leaf = MiMC(Secret, In.Value, In.Owner) in Define and start the Merkle chain from it instead of the free Path[0].

options.label: Option A — derive the leaf in-circuit
options.diff:
-	cur := c.Path[0]
+	h.Reset()
+	h.Write(c.Secret, c.In.Value, c.In.Owner)
+	leaf := h.Sum()
+	api.AssertIsEqual(c.Path[0], leaf)
+	cur := leaf

poc.command: GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off timeout 600 go -C <out>/worktree-1 test -run PoC_1 -count=1 ./circuit/
poc.output_excerpt: attack k=1: proof VERIFIED ... attack k=2: proof VERIFIED ... control: wrong nullifier rejected; control: wrong path rejected; sanity: honest transfer accepted; PASS

refuter.reasoning: transfer.go:50-56 starts from cur := c.Path[0] and never compares it with a hash of Secret, In.Value, In.Owner or Index; transfer.go:47-48 binds the nullifier only to free witnesses; Pool.sol:39-51 checks root, nullifier freshness and the proof, then pays value. No blocking constraint found.

records.title: Index is not tied to the Merkle path, so one note has unlimited nullifiers
records.description: Any note holder derives a new nullifier per Index, because the Merkle fold never reads Index; the fixed left order also blocks right-child leaves.
records.proof: Same Secret, Path, Root, In=Out=1000: Index=1 and Index=2 give nf=MiMC(s,1) and nf=MiMC(s,2); both solve and both Groth16 proofs verify. Control: Index=2 with MiMC(s,1) is rejected at transfer.go:48. Completeness: leaf L1 with Path=[L1,L0,N1,N2] under root H(H(H(L0,L1),N1),N2) is rejected at transfer.go:56.
records.impact: A note holder withdraws the same note any number of times, even after the leaf fix; honest notes at right-child positions cannot be withdrawn.

gates.executes: Index appears only at transfer.go:47 and transfer.go:82; the loop at transfer.go:51-55 hashes (cur, Path[i]) without it.
gates.impact: Double spend: Pool.sol:40 sees a fresh nullifier for the same note.

fix.summary: Decompose Index into Depth bits, use each bit to order (cur, Path[i]) with api.Select, and keep nf = MiMC(Secret, Index).

options.label: Option A — direction bits from Index
options.diff:
+	idxBits := bits.ToBinary(api, c.Index, bits.WithNbDigits(Depth))
 	for i := 1; i < len(c.Path); i++ {
 		h.Reset()
-		h.Write(cur, c.Path[i])
+		left := api.Select(idxBits[i-1], c.Path[i], cur)
+		right := api.Select(idxBits[i-1], cur, c.Path[i])
+		h.Write(left, right)
 		cur = h.Sum()
 	}

options.label: Option B — derive the nullifier from the bound leaf

records.title: Pool calls a verifyProof signature the gnark verifier does not have
records.description: Pool calls verifyProof(bytes,uint256[7]), but the gnark-generated verifier exposes verifyProof(uint256[8],uint256[7]) and no fallback, so every withdrawal reverts.
records.proof: Generated Verifier.sol from `go run ./cmd/setup` in a scratch worktree, deployed as GenVerifier with Pool(gen); withdraw reverts with empty revert data (selector miss) and leaves the nullifier unspent; the generated selector exists and reverts with ProofInvalid on a zero proof; control with a mock implementing Pool's ABI succeeds.
records.impact: No withdrawal succeeds against a genuine gnark verifier, so deposits stay locked until the owner deploys an unreviewed adapter.

gates.executes: Selectors differ (bytes vs uint256[8]); the generated contract (solidity.go:680-687) has no fallback.
gates.reachable: Every withdraw call against the exported verifier.
gates.unprivileged: Hits every honest user; no special actor needed.
gates.impact: Completeness: the core withdrawal flow is bricked; the owner can only work around it with setVerifier and custom code.

fix.summary: Declare verifyProof(uint256[8] calldata proof, uint256[7] calldata input) in IVerifier and pass the proof as uint256[8] from withdraw.

options.label: Option A — match the generated ABI
options.diff:
-    function verifyProof(bytes calldata proof, uint256[7] calldata input) external view;
+    function verifyProof(uint256[8] calldata proof, uint256[7] calldata input) external view;

refuter.reasoning: Pool.sol:5 and :49 use verifyProof(bytes,uint256[7]); gnark v0.14.0 backend/groth16/bn254/solidity.go:680-687 emits verifyProof(uint256[8],uint256[7]) and no fallback; backend/solidity export options change only pragma and hash. Liveness bug, not a soundness break.

records.title: gnark v0.14.0 is affected by three std advisories; emulated arithmetic is used
records.description: gnark v0.14.0 matches GHSA-3mvx-pp85-pm65, GHSA-7fx8-hmgc-82jp and GHSA-fwf3-jmp7-gmrj; SigCircuit uses std/math/emulated, a GHSA-3mvx component.
records.proof: go.mod requires github.com/consensys/gnark v0.14.0; circuit/sig.go:34-38 calls emulated.NewField[emparams.Secp256k1Fr] and f.Mul (GHSA-3mvx component, fixed v0.16.2). ECDSA/fake-GLV (GHSA-7fx8) and pairing G2 (GHSA-fwf3) components are not imported.
records.impact: SigCircuit's emulated arithmetic runs on std code with known unbound hint outputs; severity is capped because no contract consumes SigCircuit.

gates.executes: Pinned version is below every fixed version.
gates.reachable: SigCircuit is a production (non-test) circuit using the affected component.
gates.unprivileged: Advisory issues are exploitable by any prover.
gates.impact: Capped at medium: SigCircuit has no on-chain consumer in the repository.

fix.summary: Upgrade gnark to v0.16.4 or later, recompile every circuit, regenerate proving and verifying keys and redeploy the verifier.

records.title: Divisibility check uses field division and drops the remainder
records.description: Any prover satisfies q·Out.Value == In.Value with a field inverse, while honest provers fail whenever Out.Value does not divide In.Value.
records.proof: In.Value=10, Out.Value=3: honest divHint gives q=3 and the solver rejects (constraint #2643: 1·9 != 10); overriding divHint with q=10·3^-1 mod r solves and the Groth16 proof verifies. Sanity In=Out=10 solves.
records.impact: Honest partial withdrawals that are not exact divisors are blocked, and the divisibility rule binds no malicious prover.

gates.executes: Only transfer.go:64 touches q; res[1] is discarded at transfer.go:63; q has no range check.
gates.reachable: Any prover overrides a hint; honest users hit it for any non-divisor amount.
gates.impact: Completeness failure for honest users plus a vacuous soundness rule.

fix.summary: Constrain q·Out.Value + rem == In.Value, range-check q and rem to 64 bits and assert rem < Out.Value, or delete the relation if no divisibility rule is intended.

options.label: Option A — full integer division
options.diff:
-	q := res[0]
-	_ = res[1]
-	api.AssertIsEqual(api.Mul(q, c.Out.Value), c.In.Value)
+	q, rem := res[0], res[1]
+	bits.ToBinary(api, q, bits.WithNbDigits(64))
+	bits.ToBinary(api, rem, bits.WithNbDigits(64))
+	api.AssertIsEqual(api.Add(api.Mul(q, c.Out.Value), rem), c.In.Value)
+	api.AssertIsLessOrEqual(api.Add(rem, 1), c.Out.Value)

options.label: Option B — drop the relation
options.diff:
-	res, err := api.Compiler().NewHint(divHint, 2, c.In.Value, c.Out.Value)
-	...
-	api.AssertIsEqual(api.Mul(q, c.Out.Value), c.In.Value)

poc.output_excerpt: control/completeness: honest hint rejects In=10, Out=3: constraint #2643 is not satisfied: 1 ⋅ 9 != 10; attack: groth16 proof with non-integer q verifies; PASS

records.title: Owner equality is gated by the prover-chosen Index
records.description: Any prover sets Index nonzero, which zeroes flag and removes the In.Owner == Out.Owner check, so Out_Owner is arbitrary.
records.proof: Index=1, In.Owner=5, Out.Owner=7 solves and its Groth16 proof verifies; control Index=0 with the same owners is rejected (constraint #4495: 1·-2 != 0); sanity Index=0 with equal owners solves.
records.impact: The public ownerKey carries no ownership guarantee; Pool ignores it today, so harm depends on future consumers.

gates.executes: transfer.go:83 multiplies the owner difference by IsZero(Index); Index is private.
gates.impact: Bounded: the circuit accepts an owner-continuity statement it does not enforce; no current fund loss.

fix.summary: Assert api.AssertIsEqual(c.In.Owner, c.Out.Owner) unconditionally (and bind In.Owner into the leaf), or gate on a public input the contract fixes.

poc.command: GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off timeout 600 go -C <out>/worktree-6 test -run PoC_6 -count=1 ./circuit/
poc.output_excerpt: control: Index=0, In.Owner=5, Out.Owner=7 rejected ... attack: groth16 proof with In.Owner=5 != Out.Owner=7 verifies; PASS

refuter.reasoning: The only owner constraint is transfer.go:82-83; Index != 0 makes it trivial; Index is otherwise constrained only by the nullifier (transfer.go:47-48), which the prover recomputes. In.Owner is also unbound to any leaf.

records.title: Non-zero check reads one limb of an unreduced emulated product
records.description: SigCircuit asserts sq.Limbs[0] != 0 on a width-checked but unreduced product, so honest non-zero amounts fail and a zero amount can pass.
records.proof: Completeness (run): honest Amount=2^32 gives sq=2^64 with limbs [0,1,0,0]; the real SigCircuit with an honest EdDSA signature is rejected (constraint #7675: 0·0 != 1), Amount=3 solves. Soundness (analysis): Amount limbs = n and a mul hint returning r=n, k=n-1 satisfy n·n = (n-1)·n + n with r.Limbs[0]=0xBFD25E8CD0364141.
records.impact: Honest provers with amounts like 2^32 cannot prove, and the non-zero amount rule does not hold; no contract consumes SigCircuit yet.

gates.executes: mulMod range-checks r only to limb width (gnark v0.14.0 field_assert.go:23-29), then sig.go:39 reads a raw limb.
gates.reachable: Honest inputs hit it at Amount=2^32; a prover can choose the representation.
gates.impact: Bounded completeness and soundness failure of SigCircuit's amount rule; no on-chain consumer.

fix.summary: Test the value, not a limb: api.AssertIsEqual(f.IsZero(sq), 0), or call f.ReduceStrict(sq) before reading limbs.

poc.command: GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off timeout 600 go -C <out>/worktree-5 test -run PoC_5 -count=1 ./circuit/
poc.output_excerpt: SigCircuit: Amount=2^32 rejected as expected: constraint #7675 is not satisfied: 0 ⋅ 0 != 1; PASS

refuter.reasoning: sig.go:38 -> mulMod (field_mul.go:229-252) returns hint remainder r packed with enforceWidth only (field.go:183-186, field_assert.go:23-29), so r < 2^256 not r < n; sig.go:39 tests a raw limb. Both directions hold.

records.title: EdDSA verification never asserts Sig.R is on the curve
records.description: gnark v0.14.0 eddsa.Verify adds Sig.R without an on-curve check, and the native Edwards formulas use DivUnchecked, which is unconstrained at 0/0 for off-curve inputs.
blockers: No PoC was run in this pass; the agent's witness was not executed.
No contract or service consumes SigCircuit proofs, so the real impact is unknown.
records.validation_plan: Add curve.AssertIsOnCurve(c.Sig.R) and curve.AssertIsOnCurve(c.PubKey.A) before eddsa.Verify, then check with a T-CONSTRAINT-MODEL test whether an off-curve R can satisfy the circuit at gnark v0.14.0 and at v0.16.4.

fix.summary: Assert Sig.R and PubKey.A on curve (and PubKey.A not small-order) in SigCircuit.Define before calling eddsa.Verify, and upgrade gnark.

records.title: Wrapped Sub in AssertIsLessOrEqual
records.description: Inventory hit FG-CMP-UNBOUNDED: change = In.Value − Out.Value may wrap before the comparison.
